whatThisIs: WHERE A RECORD GOES WHEN SOMEBODY PRESSES SAVE, declared ONCE, and asserted against BOTH places
a record can be created from.
The owner's words, which are the whole of R7: "the records created through the design and
prototype workshop as well as through the record pages should utilise the same endpoints and
should be saved in the same manner, which is why there should be parity contract between the
integrated record pages and the record pages as well".
A record has TWO doors. The STANDALONE record pages (/tools/new, /artisans/[id]/edit, the
handset's own create and edit screens) and the INTEGRATED surfaces inside a design workshop (the
dialog a stage's reference picker opens, and the record form a stage EMBEDS in the page). This
file declares the endpoint, the payload keys, the destination rule, the validation and the
offline queue shape ONCE, and the enforcing test holds both doors to all five.
IT ALSO HOLDS THE SHAPE OF THE CONTROL ITSELF, and that half is not about R7 at all. R2 is two
dropdowns and never three; the third control was deleted in this release and the two labels are
asserted here, on both clients, in order, with the retired ones forbidden by name. That is what
stops R2 regressing on the seventh form somebody adds.
whyAContractAndNotJustTests: BECAUSE THE PARITY IS TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION TODAY, AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY IT NEEDS WRITING DOWN.
Measured on 2026-09-16 before a line was written: there is no second endpoint. The integrated
surfaces mount the REAL record form — `components/designworkshop/InlineRecordDialog.tsx` says so
in its own header ("IT MOUNTS THE REAL FORM, NOT A SIMPLER ONE") and
`components/designworkshop/StageRecordEmbed.tsx` was written for it ("this mounts the ACTUAL
COMPONENT … the same one its own route mounts, with nothing removed, reordered or restyled").
declares no record-creating route of any kind: every POST under `/design-workshops` is a
dictation, an AI layer, a report or an export.
SO THE DEFECT R7 GUARDS AGAINST IS NOT PRESENT, AND THE CONTRACT IS A RATCHET RATHER THAN A FIX.
The thing that would break it is the obvious next feature: a "quick create" with four boxes
inside a stage, so a designer does not have to meet the full artisan form in a room. Both hosts'
headers argue against it at length and neither argument is enforced by anything. A second write
path would be a second answer to what an artisan IS, drifting from the first, and the records it
made would be the ones missing the fields nobody could see were missing.
WHAT A TEST ALONE COULD NOT DO, which is the reason this is a declaration and not thirty
assertions: the assertions have to know which differences between the two doors are LEGITIMATE.
Three are (see `declaredDifferences`), and a test with no declaration beside it either fails on
all three or is written so loosely it would pass over a fourth nobody argued for.

why: The files that mount a record form, per client, per door. Spelled out rather than globbed,
because the thing this list protects against is a THIRD host arriving with its own form — and a
glob over "files that mount ArtisanForm" would grow to include it the moment it existed.
A DOOR IS NOT A ROUTE. `StageRecordEmbed` is neither a page nor a modal: it renders the record
form inline underneath a stage's picker, with the stage's own questions in the form's
`footerFields` slot. It is a third host with two hosts' worth of chrome differences and zero
differences in what it saves, which is the distinction this whole file is about.
ONE MOUNT SHARED BY TWO HOSTS. `InlineRecordForm` lives in `InlineRecordDialog.tsx` and both
hosts render it: which of the four components answers a `refModel`, fetching the record for
an edit and not mounting until it is in hand, refusing to seed a parent over an existing
record. What differs is the chrome — a `FieldDialog` here, a panel section there — and
whether the host closes on save. A second copy of that mount is the failure
`forms/inlineRecordHost.ts` already exists to prevent, one level up.
THE ANCHOR MATCHES TWICE, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE FILE RATHER THAN A LOOSE ANCHOR. There
are two `is Screen.Create -> when (s.mode)` blocks in MainActivity.kt: one maps the mode to a
`NavDestination` for the nav rail, the other mounts the forms. The enforcing test reads EVERY
match and requires that exactly one of them mounts all five forms — which is a stronger check
than a hand-tightened anchor, because a second create screen mounting different forms fails it.
ONE HOST, AND IT REUSES THE APP'S OWN EDIT LOADER WHOLESALE. `DwInlineRecordDialog` mounts
`ArtisanForm` / `ProductForm` / `ToolForm` / `ProcessForm` for a create and calls
`EditScreen` for an edit — "which is one place for that decision rather than two that can
disagree", in its own words. The handset has no third host: there is no stage EMBED on the
phone, only the dialog.

android.mountRefuses: onSubmit = { error("An open edit must PATCH the interview, never create a second one.") }

note: THE ONE RECORD WITH NO INTEGRATED DOOR, and that is a fact about the stage registry rather
than a gap in this contract: `INLINE_CREATABLE` on both clients is Artisan, Product, Tool and
Process, because those are the four reference models a stage field can point at. There is no
`refModel` of `QuestionnaireInterview`, so no picker can offer to create one.
ITS WEB FORM IS CREATE-ONLY, which is why `update` is null there: an interview is corrected
through the review panel, never re-opened in the capture form. The handset DOES edit one in
place, and refuses to queue that edit offline for a stated reason — see `declaredDifferences`.

why: ONE FUNCTION PER CLIENT STANDS BETWEEN A RECORD FORM AND THE NETWORK, and both doors go
through it. That is the whole of "saved in the same manner": not that the two hosts happen to
call the same endpoint today, but that neither of them has anywhere else to call it from.
THE ASSERTION IS A COUNT AND NOT A PRESENCE. "The form calls `saveOrQueue`" is satisfied by a
form that calls it once and `apiFetch("/artisans", {method: "POST"})` beside it for the
embedded case. What is held is that each form has EXACTLY ONE record write and that it is this
one.
TWO CALLS AND NOT ONE, and the shape is the browser's inverted rather than a second design.
`trySaveOffline` answers null when the device is online and the form then calls the repository's
own create/update; `saveOrQueue` makes the same decision inside itself. The consequence that
matters is identical on both: a 4xx is never queued (“the server saw it and said no”), and a
request that never reached the server always is.
AND THE HANDSET SPELLS THE OFFLINE HALF TWO WAYS, WHICH IS MEASURED HERE RATHER THAN TIDIED.
`trySaveOffline` is the short form — it takes a `MediaCaptureState` and builds the media specs
itself — and the artisan, product and craft forms use it. The tool, process and interview forms
call `repository.queueOfflineEntry` directly because they have media the short form cannot
describe: a tool routes graph-paper shots into the same `uris` list and must carry the grid
`purpose` with each FILE, a process attaches media per numbered step, an interview carries a
clip per question. Both land in `WorkshopRepository.queueOffline` and both write the same
`PendingEntry`, which is the only thing this contract is about. `queueVia` per record says
which, so a form that quietly stops queueing is a red test rather than a silent loss of a day's
fieldwork.
AND ONE FORM'S CREATE IS INJECTED AT THE MOUNT. `QuestionnaireForm` takes
`onSubmit: suspend (QuestionnaireInterviewCreateRequest) -> String`, and its TWO mounts now
supply two DIFFERENT things. The create screen supplies `repository.createQuestionnaireInterview`;
`InterviewEditLoader` supplies an `error(…)`, because that mount always passes `editing` and the
form routes on it, so its `onSubmit` can only ever be reached by a refactor — and what it used to
hold was the wrong verb, correctly typed. `createVia` per record says which shape to expect,
`mountSupplies` pins the create and `mountRefuses` pins the refusal, so neither can quietly
become the other.
THAT MOVE WAS A DECISION AND NOT A FIX, in the sense `maintenance` below draws. `mountSupplies`
read `onSubmit = { repository.createQuestionnaireInterview(it).id }` — the edit loader's dead
line, and the only place that exact spelling ever appeared in the tree. So this contract was
green on the strength of the one mount that must never create, and would have gone red the day
somebody deleted that line for exactly the right reason. It now names a line inside the create
mount, which is the mount the claim was always about.
THE TWO KEYS THAT CARRY THE WORKSHOP, in every record body on both clients and through both
doors. R1 keeps both tables and both nullable foreign keys; what the picker guarantees is that
AT MOST ONE of them is ever non-empty.
BOTH ARE ALWAYS SENT, AND THAT IS THE HALF THAT LOOKS REDUNDANT AND IS NOT. The update routes
dump with `exclude_unset=True`, so a key omitted means "leave the stored value alone" — and the
single edit that could never be saved would be the one that UN-FILES a record. An explicit null
is what empties the column. The handset says the same thing in its own vocabulary through
`PendingEntry.clearedLinkKeys`, because a queued body is built once and replayed later.
NEITHER CLIENT SENDS THE TYPE. There is no `workshopType`, `workshopTypeId` or `workshopKind`
key in any record body and there must not be (R3): the workshop the record names already
carries its own type, and a second copy beside the record could disagree with its own source
the first time somebody corrects it. That is asserted as a negative, per form, per client.
R3, DECLARED ONCE PER CLIENT AND NOWHERE ELSE. The type box chooses which of the record's two
columns the chosen workshop is written to, by the type row's own `routesToDesignWorkshop` flag:
true fills `designWorkshopId` and blanks `workshopId`, false does the reverse.
READ THE FLAG, NEVER THE KEY. A `key === "DESIGN_PROTOTYPE_DEVELOPMENT"` test in a picker is
the bug the constant's own doc comment exists to prevent: an administrator may add a second
design-workshop-backed programme, and nothing in the database constrains "exactly one true
row". The key is licensed in three places on each client — the import, the offline FLOOR (which
has no served row to read a flag off), and NAMING a retired programme a record is still filed
under — and every SERVED row is read through the flag.
IT LIVES IN THE PICKER AND NOT IN THE FORMS, which is what makes the two doors identical for
free: a form reads two ids off one control and writes them into two keys. A form that re-derived
the routing would be a sixth copy of this rule, and the integrated host would be the seventh.

expressions: fun workshopId(): String? = if (routesToDesignWorkshop) null else field.value()
fun designWorkshopId(): String? = if (routesToDesignWorkshop) design.value() else null

why: R5. Both branches of both clients draw a "no workshop" row and it is a real answer that
reaches the wire. `NO_FIELD_WORKSHOP` is the one wording, on both halves, on both clients:
the design half's own default ("Not filed under a design workshop") is right when it is one
of two boxes and wrong when it is the only one, so the picker overrides it.
notLinkedSurvives.label: Not linked to a workshop

why: R4 IS A RULE FOR A NEW RECORD AND FOR NOTHING ELSE. On an EDIT the type box opens on whichever
type routes the way the STORED columns already do, and "the most recent workshop this account
can reach" is never applied over it. Getting that wrong re-files historic records under
whatever is newest, invisibly, on the next save of a form somebody merely opened.
Both clients pin it the same way and both name the function: the routing is derived from the
two stored ids, and `isEdit` blocks each half's own prefill.
R2: EXACTLY TWO BOXES ON A RECORD FORM, IN THIS ORDER, WITH THESE WORDS, ON BOTH CLIENTS.
The third control is gone. It was a `WORKSHOP_KIND` filter whose own hint read "Narrows the
workshops below. It is not saved on this record." — a box that changed a list and saved nothing,
borrowed from a vocabulary that answers stage 1 of a design workshop's own questionnaire. The
components that drew it (`frontend/components/forms/DesignWorkshopCascade.tsx` on the web, the
kind half of `ui/DesignWorkshopPicker.kt` on the handset) were DELETED, not merely unmounted:
an unmounted component is a control the next form will find and use.
COUNTED STRUCTURALLY AND NOT BY LABEL. A label check goes green over a third box called
anything; what is asserted is that each record form mounts exactly ONE picker element, that the
picker draws exactly two labelled boxes, and that no record form reaches the halves directly.

deletedComponents.why: The web's kind box plus the design-workshop box. Deleted 2026-09-16 once its last two callers (the misc-media form and the interview form) were converted.
Nine assertions pinning the cascade, five of them about the `workshopKind` narrowing R2 removes. Deleted with the component it described rather than left red.
The handset twin, seven of whose assertions describe the kind filter. Its live rulings were re-asserted in `ui/WorkshopPickerTest.kt` before it was deleted.

why: NAMES THAT MUST NOT COME BACK, asserted across both client trees rather than per form,
because the way a third box returns is a helper that survives the form that used it.
`workshopKind` is deliberately NOT on this list: it is a real column on `DesignWorkshop`,
answered in stage 1 of its own questionnaire and read by the workshop list, the annual plan
and the stage registry. What is forbidden is a RECORD FORM narrowing by it.
THE ONE PRE-FLIGHT A RECORD FORM RUNS BEFORE IT SAVES, and it runs on both doors because it
lives in the picker rather than in the host. `confirmSubmission()` asks
`GET /workshops/{id}/submission-check` and surfaces two answers a researcher has to learn
BEFORE the save rather than after: that they are not on a curated workshop's roster, and that
the workshop's submission window has closed (which is accepted, but pinned to PENDING and
flagged so only an admin can approve it).
IT IS A NO-OP WHEN THE TYPE ROUTES AT A DESIGN WORKSHOP, on both clients, and that is not a
weakening of the gate. The window and the assignment roster are properties of a `Workshop`; a
`DesignWorkshop` has neither, and nothing is being filed against the ordinary workshop the
field half may still be holding. Asking anyway would raise the late-submission dialog about a
workshop the save will not name.
ASSERTED AS "CALLED BEFORE THE WRITE" AND NOT MERELY "CALLED": a pre-flight after the POST is
a confirmation dialog about work already saved.
THE QUEUE SHAPE IS PART OF "SAVED IN THE SAME MANNER", and it is the half a reviewer skips.
A record created in a courtyard with no signal is not saved by the same code path as one
created at a desk — it is serialised, banked, and replayed hours later against a server that
has moved on. If the integrated door queued a different shape, or did not queue at all, the two
doors would agree online and diverge in exactly the conditions this application exists for.
ONE ENTRY SHAPE PER CLIENT AND BOTH DOORS WRITE IT. Neither host disables queueing and neither
adds a field: the entry is built by the FORM, which is the same component on both doors.
THE ONE THING THE DIALOG ADDS IS A MESSAGE, NOT A SHAPE. `onQueued` exists because
`OutboxBanner` sits at the top of the protected layout, behind `FieldDialog`'s overlay on a body
whose scroll the dialog has locked — so a queued save inside a dialog was indistinguishable from
one that failed, which is how a designer banks three copies of one artisan. It changes what the
host SAYS and nothing about what is stored.
THE HANDSET'S ONE EXTRA FIELD, AND IT HAS NO BROWSER TWIN BECAUSE A BROWSER HAS NO OUTBOX
ENTRY TO CARRY IT. A queued body is built once and sent later, so it has to record WHY a
workshop box was empty: `UNFILED_BY_CHOICE` (somebody cleared it — reaches the server as an
explicit null) or `UNFILED_NO_OPTIONS` (the picker had nothing in it — sends nothing, so a
stored link is not destroyed by a device that simply could not list the workshops).
The browser settles the same question at submit time, in the payload, because it is never
more than one request away from the server. Same outcome, different moment.
DIFFERENCES BETWEEN THE TWO DOORS, OR BETWEEN THE TWO CLIENTS, THAT ARE LEGITIMATE — each with
the reason, and each ASSERTED so it cannot go stale.
WHY THE ROWS ARE THEMSELVES CHECKED. This is `openDrifts`' ratchet from
`shared/questionnaire-form-contract.json`, turned the other way up. There a row names a defect
that must stop being true; here a row names a DIFFERENCE that is allowed to be true, and the
test asserts it still is. Either way a row cannot rot: the moment somebody converges the two
sides, the assertion fails and says to delete the row. A list of licensed exceptions that
nothing checks reads as a considered account long after the product has moved, and the next
person widens it.
"DECLARED, NOT TOLERATED SILENTLY" IS THE WHOLE POINT. A difference nobody wrote down is
indistinguishable from a bug nobody noticed.
THE INTEGRATED DOOR FILLS THE WORKSHOP BOX IN; THE STANDALONE DOOR PROBES FOR IT. A stage's
reference picker knows which ordinary `Workshop` the design workshop is linked to, so it
seeds that id and the picker treats it exactly as a STORED id: the type box opens on the
ordinary-workshop side with that workshop chosen, and the most-recent probe and the carry bag
are kept off it.
IT IS NOT A DIFFERENT SAVE. The seed lands in the same control a designer would have used,
showing the same name, and they can change it before saving — `inlineRecordHost.ts` requires
that of every seed ("a seed is only allowed to be a DEFAULT they can see, never a claim made
behind the form"). The endpoint, the keys, the routing rule and the queue are untouched.
WHAT IT FIXES IS WORSE THAN WHAT IT COSTS: a tool created from a workshop-scoped picker and
filed against a different sitting is a tool that picker can never show again, and the
designer who created it is looking at an empty control seconds later.
`DwInlineSeed` carries an artisan and nothing else, so the handset's integrated door leaves
the workshop question to the form's own defaulting. The browser seeds it (row above).
THE TWO ARE BOTH DEFENSIBLE AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS WRITTEN DOWN AS A DECISION, which is why
this row exists rather than a fix. Android's inline host states the principle — "asserting a
parent this picker never saw the form choose would be a claim about whose product it is" —
and applies it to the workshop as well as the artisan; the browser draws the line at values
the designer can see and change. Converging them is a product call and not a defect: the
handset's default (the most recent workshop the account can reach) is a good answer, and the
browser's (the workshop this design workshop is linked to) is a better one.
IT CHANGES NO PART OF THE SAVE. Same endpoint, same keys, same routing, same queue — only
which workshop is already in the box when the form opens, in a control that says what it
holds.

androidFormContains.text: A correction to an interview cannot be saved on this device.

why: THE HANDSET EDITS AN INTERVIEW IN PLACE AND WILL NOT QUEUE THAT EDIT OFFLINE. It refuses, in
the room, with the answers still on screen, and says why.
The reason is `responsesToSend`: it is a DIFF computed against what the server held when the
form was opened, and `QuestionnaireInterviewUpdateRequest` reads a present `responses` as
"replace". Replaying that diff hours later, against a sitting a second interviewer may have
added answers to, would drop theirs without either person being told. `artisanIds` has the
same shape and the same hazard.
THE BROWSER NEVER MEETS THIS because its capture form is create-only — an interview is
corrected through the review panel — so there is no web behaviour to match. Closing it
properly needs the interview's own version as a precondition, which is what the custom
questionnaire's write already does, and not a queue.

rows.between: record forms and the two forms that are not
why: TWO SURFACES HAVE ONE DESTINATION EACH, SO THEY DRAW ONE BOX AND NO TYPE BOX. Both clients
agree, and the agreement is new: the browser drew the retired cascade's TWO boxes on the
misc-media form until 2026-09-16 while the handset had already dropped to one.
CRAFT: `model Craft` in `backend/prisma/schema.prisma` has `workshopId` and no
`designWorkshopId`. A type box there would offer six rows, five of which could change nothing
and the sixth of which would route at a column that does not exist.
MISCELLANEOUS MEDIA: `MediaFile` has BOTH columns, but `MediaCompleteRequest`
(backend/app/schemas/media.py) declares only `designWorkshopId`, and so do `frontend/lib`'s
upload body and Android's `ApiModels.MediaCompleteRequest`. So this is a WIRE gap and not a
data one, and the fix is three request shapes rather than a form: add `workshopId` to all
three and both mounts become the two-box picker like the other five. Until then a type box
would offer five types whose answer the upload physically cannot carry — which is the exact
complaint the retired kind box earned.
NEITHER IS A RECORD FORM FOR THE PURPOSES OF R2, and saying so here is what stops the next
reader 'fixing' them into three-box forms or reading their single box as a regression.

notCoveredHere: WHAT THIS FILE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DECLARE, each because it is already one register somewhere
else and a second copy here would be the failure this file exists to prevent:
* WHAT THE INTERVIEW FORM ASKS FOR, field by field, in screen order, on both clients and in all
three walkthrough registers. That is `shared/questionnaire-form-contract.json`, which is the
authority on the SHAPE of that one form; this file is the authority on what any record form
DOES with the answer. The two overlap on exactly two rows — "Type of workshop" and
"Workshop" — and both read them from the same components rather than from each other.
* THE WORKSHOP-TYPE TABLE ITSELF: its columns, its five endpoints, the admin screen and the
refusal that names how many workshops are filed under a type. That is
* WHO MAY CREATE A WORKSHOP (R6). `backend/tests/test_workshop_creation_rights.py` holds the
route, both clients' controls and the refusal sentence, in 29 tests.
* THE OFFLINE QUEUE'S BEHAVIOUR — retry, skew, dangling references, media replay. Both clients
have their own suites for it. What is declared here is only its SHAPE, and only so far as the
maintenance: WHEN A RECORD FORM GAINS A NEW WAY TO BE SAVED, this file changes in the same commit. A third
host, a second endpoint, a form that writes without the picker — each of those is a decision, and
a decision that arrives as a green test is a decision nobody made.
THE ORDER MATTERS AND IT IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE. An edit that changes a client to match this file
is a FIX; an edit that changes this file to match a client is a DECISION. They should not look
alike in a diff, and the second should never be the way a red test is turned green.
IF THIS FILE IS EVER RED BECAUSE A DIFFERENCE IS GONE, the row in `declaredDifferences` says so
in its failure message and the edit is to delete the row. That is the good direction.
